Subject: RFP: LLM evaluation & labeling partner — initial packet

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're kicking off a formal sourcing for an LLM evaluation & labeling partner to support a set of prompt-eval projects and ongoing human labeling for our quality monitoring pipeline. Attached is our RFP/spec packet (Redwood_RFP_Specs.pdf) which includes sample prompt sets, target SLAs, and expected monthly volume.

High-level asks:
- 10k labeled examples per month for 6 months (with scaling options)
- Structured prompt-evaluation support: annotation schema, inter-annotator agreement (IAA) reports, and sample-level flags
- A lightweight consult for prompt-set design and evaluation metric calibration
- Fixed-price SOW options + hourly consulting for ad-hoc eval projects

Timeline: Please confirm availability for SOW + pricing proposal by EOD next Friday (2026-07-09). Procurement will need a draft SOW and SOC2 evidence.

Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Specs.pdf (attached)

Subject: Re: RFP: LLM evaluation & labeling partner — initial packet

Anna —

Quick technical clarifications from infra/ML side (copying Monica and Lauren):

> 1) For prompt-eval tasks, do you require pairwise comparisons or absolute rubric labels?

We prefer absolute rubric labels with a small set of pairwise checks for calibration. The rubric will need to support: factuality, instruction-following, harmful content flag, and response utility (0-3). We'll provide an initial rubric but expect back-and-forth for edge cases.

> 2) Expected median sequence length for prompts/outputs (tokens)?

Median prompt length ~40 tokens, median model output ~120 tokens. But there is a heavy tail for long-form generation (up to ~800 tokens) for a small fraction (~5%). Please plan sampling and batching that tolerates variable lengths.

> 3) Do you need on-prem/local data handling, or is redacted/PII-free content acceptable for your initial pilots?

For pilot, redacted/PII-free content is fine. For production we may need VPC/private deployment options; include notes on operational controls and KMS integration in your SOW.

Also: we will want IAA reports weekly and tooling that lets us re-run evaluations against new model versions. Can you outline your tooling/infrastructure for dataset versioning and re-eval workflows?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Applied ML — Serving & Evaluation, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Anna —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and Marcus for the details. A few procurement-specific notes:

- Please provide two pricing options: (A) committed fixed-price SOW for 6 months (10k labels/mo) with unit price per label and milestone payments; (B) time-and-materials estimate for ad-hoc consulting (hours x rate).
- Include SLA targets for turnaround (48-hour standard, 24-hour expedited), accuracy/IAA targets, and proposed remedies (credits) for missed SLAs.
- We will require a draft SOW and SOC2 evidence to move to signature. Legal (cc Neha) may request some redlines around IP and data retention — please flag any clauses you cannot accept.
- Procurement deadline: we need a signed SOW or approved PO by 2026-07-23 to keep the pilot schedule.

Attaching the RFP spec again for reference. Could you also include a sample annotation schema and two anonymized example labels so our reviewers can validate format?

Related links: HubSpot deal HS-34512 (tracking), please include that ID in your proposal.

Thanks — would like to pick a vendor by 2026-07-16 if possible.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Monica / team —

Thanks — attaching a tailored SOW outline (LabelCraft_SOW_Outline.docx) and a short capability appendix. Highlights:
- Fixed-price option (A): $48,000/month for 10k labels, includes weekly IAA reports, tooling access, and one consult day/month for rubric tuning. 6-month committed term.
- T&M option (B): $210/hr for consulting; label work billed per-label if volume varies.
- SLA: standard turnaround 48 hours, expedited 24 hours (premium); IAA target >= 0.82 with escalation path.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence under NDA; will include in the formal proposal.

I created a draft DocuSign packet for the SOW and sent the link to your procurement contacts. Preview here: https://www.docusign.com/rafts/abc123

Attached: LabelCraft_Capabilities.pdf, LabelCraft_SOW_Outline.docx (both attached).

Let us know if you'd like a short technical demo of our labeling tool next week.

Best,
Anna Cho
Head of Partnerships, LabelCraft AI
